paper_metadata.title: Application of quantum Monte Carlo integration to Markovian backward stochastic differential equations

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical Quantum Least-Squares Monte Carlo (QLSM) algorithm for Markovian BSDEs, using quantum Monte Carlo integration to estimate regression matrix entries and regression targets at each time step.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Least-Squares Monte Carlo (QLSM) with quantum Monte Carlo integration

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical BSDE state X_t is discretized in time and represented through fixed-point quantum arithmetic; basis functions e_i^j(X_ti^N) are evaluated via quantum access oracles. Brownian increments are sampled through quantum access to the normal distribution.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve Markovian BSDE dX_t = b(t,X_t)dt + sigma(t,X_t)dW_t, dY_t = -f(t,X_t,Y_t,Z_t)dt + Z_t dW_t, with terminal condition Y_T = g(X_T), by least-squares regression over basis functions and quantum estimation of expectations.

problem_instance.description: General Markovian BSDE pricing/risk-management setting; no specific numerical instance, asset set, or market dataset is provided.

dataset_specification.description: No empirical dataset; abstract BSDE coefficients b, sigma, f, g are assumed to satisfy Lipschitz/Hölder conditions.

problem_instance.classical_preprocessing: Time discretization with step h = T/N; least-squares regression basis selection; Euler-Maruyama forward simulation for X.
problem_instance.classical_postprocessing: Classical inversion of estimated regression matrices eA_i and reconstruction of Y_ti via basis expansion.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct regression matrices and target vectors from simulated paths; compute matrix inverses classically.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Use classical computer to compute eA_i^{-1}, regression coefficients eBeta_i,l, and final Y_0 estimate.

classical_baselines.value: estimated via chebyshev's inequality; same theorem framework as quantum but without quantum speedup

speedup_claims.factor: speedup over classical Monte Carlo estimation; quantum Monte Carlo integration gives quadratic-type improvement in ε dependence
speedup_claims.conditions: under the quantum arithmetic model, quantum access assumptions, and using QMCI for expectation estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the speedup is compared with the cost estimate in [5] and notes that the result is theoretical; no empirical benchmark is provided.
